enchantment_lore.ethereal_enchantments:o: With enchantments fully understood, most ancients were satisfied with the magic they had unlocked. However, some of them were not satisfied and wanted more. In an attempt to bypass the normal laws of enchanting, this splinter group's plan backfired, creating the Curse of Obliteration. This Curse is so unstable that it decays enchantments when the tool is held by a living thing.

Compatible with: Anything

When an item is held in a player's inventory, the enchantments on that item decay over time, level by level.
enchantment_lore.ethereal_enchantments:a: The development of potions in ancient times led to a renaissance—but it also led to wars much more destructive than anything that had come before. In an attempt to counteract potion-wielding warriors, ancient enchanters developed Affliction, an enchantment that transfers negative status effects from the wielder to the victim.

Compatible with: Melee Weapons and Tridents

Transfers negative status effects from the attacker to the victim. Higher levels transfer a larger proportion of the effect.

Not all enchantments are created equal—some are created on accident. Unbreaking is one of the most essential enchantments to modern life, but it is not perfect. When an Unbreaking enchantment fails to materialize, the end result is the Curse of Atrophy, a curse which increases the rate at which durability is lost.

Compatible with: Anything

Increases the rate at which durability is lost. Each level corresponds to one extra loss of durability upon use.
enchantment_lore.ethereal_enchantments:b: Sharpness increases damage output, but it doesn't increase it enough for some. Smite and Bane of Arthropods were developed to address Sharpness' limitations, but they only work against certain enemies. In an attempt to bring Smite and Bane of Arthropods' increased damage output, Brutality was crafted. Brutality deals more damage than Sharpness against all enemies—at the cost of also damaging the wielder.

Compatible with: Melee Weapons

Increases damage output by 2.5 x level, but damages the wielder by 1 + (1 x level) (magic damage) for every attack.
enchantment_lore.ethereal_enchantments:h: The sea harbors many horrors, but to sailors there is one terror greater than them all: storms. Hurricane captures the ocean's natural meteorological ferocity by creating a large wind burst at the location of every Trident thrown.

Compatible with: Trident

Creates a wind burst at the location of thrown tridents (hitting blocks or entities) and when attacking entities in melee combat.
enchantment_lore.ethereal_enchantments:k: The earliest enchanters ran into a bottleneck when first developing their craft—without a source of experience, they could not enchant. To address this limitation, Knowledge was created—by interfacing with the intrinsic magic of the world, this enchantment increases the rate at which experience is produced by mining and slaying enemies.

Compatible with: Melee weapons and tools

Increases experience dropped by blocks and entities. Each level adds 1/3 as much experience.
enchantment_lore.ethereal_enchantments:m: Efficiency and Fortune had created a surplus of precious metals and minerals, but iron and diamond alone cannot build civilizations. The production of raw materials had plateaued—pickaxes simply could not become faster by conventional means. To address this, Momentum was created, which allows the wielder to build up a rhythm, increasing the rate at which they mine a single material—but it completely resets upon mining anything else.

Compatible with: Mining Tools

Increases the rate at which you mine as you continuously mine the same block. Changing the block you mine resets your efficiency increase. Higher levels increase the rate at which the increase occurs.
enchantment_lore.ethereal_enchantments:f: The first beacon revolutionized mining forever, as it allowed for the instant quarrying of stone. But below the stone layer, the compacted deepslate still proved impervious to instamining techniques—pickaxes can only swing so fast due to their size and weight. Knowing this, an enchantment was made to reduce the weight of tools to allow for faster mining—however, this enchantment, Frenzy, only works when the tool is close to breaking.

Compatible with: Mining Tools

Increases the rate at which you mine as your tool's durability decreases.
enchantment_lore.ethereal_enchantments:b: Not all enchantments are made equal—some are silly mistakes. When experimenting with random enchanting techniques, an ancient enchanter accidentally happened upon a curse that coats tools in a slippery substance. While not immediately detrimental, this slipperiness gives a chance for the tool to be randomly dropped.

Compatible with: Tools and Weapons (no Armor)

Causes a small chance to drop the enchanted tool or weapon upon use
enchantment_lore.ethereal_enchantments:u: Ancient enchanters were fascinated with what they had identified as an intrinsic field of magic that covered all three known worlds. It was believed that directly interfacing with this field of magic could create enchantments much more powerful than ever seen before. The earliest attempt to create such an enchantment made the tool constantly "touch" the field—however, rather than adding power, this only added drag, making the enchanted tool much more cumbersome to use. While the proof of concept was achieved, the attempt released the Curse of Unwieldiness onto the world, which makes weapons and tools unusable unless wielded by both hands at once.

Compatible with: Tools and Weapons (no Armor)

Drops the enchanted tool or weapon on attempt to use it when the offhand is occupied.
enchantment_lore.ethereal_enchantments:s: Unlike the modern day, ancient enchanters and alchemists saw little overlap in their fields of study, despite both being magical in nature. In an attempt to prove that alchemy and enchanting are not two wholly separate disciplines and rather two expressions of magic, an ancient enchanter drew upon early knowledge of alchemy to create Stunning, an enchantment that applies the potion effects of Slowness and Weakness on victims. This enchantment was used extensively in the upcoming wars spurred on by the golden age of alchemy.

Compatible with: Swords, Axes, and Spears

Inflicts victims with Slowness and Weakness.
enchantment_lore.ethereal_enchantments:v: Despite being recognized as alchemical in nature today, Poison is so basal as to not be identified as magical until modern times. As such, despite a historical gap between enchanting and alchemy, Poison had been experimented with by early enchanters much longer than many other alchemical enchantments. Venomous was created by studying the magic found in Cave Spiders, and inflicts poison upon victims.

Compatible with: Swords, Axes, and Spears

Inflicts victims with Poison.
